html:
Asunción is the capital of Paraguay, founded on the Paraguay River on 15 August 1537 as a Spanish fort. It is one of the oldest cities in South America.

The first Spanish settlement at Buenos Aires was abandoned in 1541, and its people moved upriver to Asunción, where the Guarani grew food and supplied women and labour. For forty years it was the centre of Spanish power in the region. Expeditions from it founded other towns, and in 1580 one of them refounded Buenos Aires. It is called the mother of cities.

As Buenos Aires grew, Asunción became a remote river town. It was the seat of independent Paraguay from 1811 and was occupied by Brazilian troops at the end of the War of the Triple Alliance. Today it is the centre of Paraguay's government and trade.
sum: Asunción is the capital of Paraguay, founded on the Paraguay River on 15 August 1537 as a Spanish fort. It is one of the oldest cities in South America.
